title: Android Auto’s endless calling loop is driving Pixel and Galaxy owners crazy
summary: Gemini knows the name to contact. Android Auto keeps asking.
body: TL;DR Some Pixel and Samsung Galaxy owners say Android Auto repeatedly asks who they want to call or message, even after they provide a contact’s name. Google’s Android Auto community specialists are collecting diagnostic details to investigate, but there’s no confirmed cause or fix yet. The complaints come as Gemini rolls out more widely in Android Auto. Making a hands-free call shouldn’t feel like an interrogation. You say a contact’s name, Android Auto places the call, and your hands stay on the wheel. But for some Pixel and Samsung Galaxy owners, that simple exchange has turned into an endless conversation with a particularly forgetful assistant. No matter how many times they repeat the name, Android Auto keeps asking the same question: Who do you want to call? The complaints have been piling up on Google’s support forums since early October, with reports involving the Pixel 10, Pixel 10 Pro, Galaxy S24, Galaxy S25 Ultra, and Galaxy S26. Both calling and texting are affected, leaving some drivers unable to reach their contacts through voice commands.

title: New Android exploit only needs you to install an app to wreck your phone
summary: Android sabotages itself next.
body: TL;DR Bitdefender researchers discovered an Android vulnerability that can trigger an endless crash loop simply by installing a specially crafted APK, potentially leaving devices unusable. The flaw exploits how Android handles ZIP compression methods, repeatedly crashing the core system_server process. Recovering may require a factory reset or manually deleting the malicious file using ADB. No in-the-wild exploitation has been identified, but the public disclosure could make it easier for threat actors to develop an exploit. Even though Android is a relatively safe operating system, with several security measures in place , threat actors’ ingenuity still keeps finding ways to exploit weaknesses. We recently shared information about malware that can empty your bank accounts in secret , and now, researchers have found a separate Android flaw that could leave your phone outright unusable. Normally, malicious apps need to request permissions and execute code to attack your device. However, researchers at Bitdefender have discovered a new vulnerability dubbed GhostMap that triggers a crash loop simply by installing a specially crafted app.

title: You can now play Switch 2 games on Android via emulators and native ports
summary: It's early days, but Switch 2 emulation and native ports show a lot of promise.
body: Credit: Oliver Cragg / Android Authority TL;DR We’ve seen the first Nintendo Switch 2 emulators on Android, although many games aren’t playable. We’ve also seen the BananaNative project, which enabled native ports of Donkey Kong Bananza and Mario Kart World on Android. It’s still early days for these projects, but it’s clear that Switch 2 emulation and native ports are progressing incredibly quickly. The Nintendo Switch 2 launched just over a year ago, but we weren’t expecting to see emulators or native ports on Android for a while yet. However, that’s exactly what’s happened in recent weeks. We’ve seen Nintendo Switch 2 emulators landing on various platforms in the last week or two, and they all seem to be ultimately based on the acclaimed Eden emulator for Nintendo Switch 1 titles. Android isn’t left out of the fun, as we’ve also seen Eden SX2A , which is based on the PokeDinner emulator for other platforms. In fact, PokeDinner is in turn based on the so-called Eglantine emulator. And that particular emulator is based on Eden-NS2, which is itself a fork of the original Eden emulator for Nintendo Switch 1 titles. Forking heck.

title: Hackers used Chrome and Snapdragon GPU flaws to hack Android phones
summary: A nasty Chrome bug let hackers break into Android phones without a tap.
body: TL;DR A security firm has found that hackers exploited a Chrome bug and a Qualcomm Adreno GPU driver flaw to infect Android phones that visited a booby-trapped website. The attack targeted Chrome versions 139 to 145 on Android and stole browser cookies, saved logins, browsing history, and Wi-Fi passwords. Both flaws had already been patched, so phones running up-to-date Chrome and security updates remained safe. Security researchers at Sekoia have detailed a mobile hacking campaign that went after Android and iPhone users through hijacked and fake websites. On Android, the attackers didn’t need victims to tap a link, install an app, or grant a permission. Opening an infected page in an outdated version of Chrome was enough. According to Sekoia’s report , the attack on Android worked in stages. First, it used a Chrome flaw tracked as CVE-2026-3910 to run code inside the browser. It then exploited CVE-2025-27038, a bug in Qualcomm’s Adreno GPU driver, to break out of Chrome’s sandbox and gain deeper access to the phone. Since Adreno graphics are found in Snapdragon chips, phones powered by Qualcomm’s silicon were the ones affected.

title: Bluetooth’s next big audio upgrade is coming, but not to your current devices
summary: Standardizing lossless and high-res audio.
body: TL;DR The Bluetooth SIG has announced HDT, a new technology that raises Bluetooth LE’s maximum bit rate from 2Mbps to 7.5Mbps. The optional Bluetooth Core 7.0 feature also promises better energy efficiency and more reliable connections across devices. Existing devices won’t automatically gain support, but the first compatible audio products could arrive in 2027. Qualcomm’s FastConnect 8800 already advertises HDT support. The Bluetooth Special Interest Group (SIG), the standards organization that oversees Bluetooth technology, today shared a significant update that could standardize lossless and high-resolution Bluetooth audio . It announced the adoption of Bluetooth High Data Throughput (HDT), which essentially increases Bluetooth LE’s maximum supported bit rate to 7.5Mbps. That’s nearly four times the current maximum. For the regular user, this should eventually mean much wider access to lossless and high-resolution audio over Bluetooth in future wireless earbuds and headphones.

body: TL;DR A new report claims Samsung may bump up the cost of its OLED panels to regain control of market prices. The company’s OLED screens are expected to cost about $10 to $20 more in 2027. Meanwhile, industry sources say the ongoing RAM crisis could continue until 2029 or 2030. The RAM crisis, driven by rising demand for AI infrastructure, has pushed prices up across the board, including smartphones. So far this year, Google and Samsung have raised prices, while other OEMs have been forced to make trade-offs to avoid that fate. But a RAM shortage may not be the only issue brands face heading into 2027, as Samsung’s OLED screens, which are used by several phone makers, could also become pricier. According to Chinese supply chain source ChannelGate, Samsung has told its suppliers that the cost of OLED panels will rise in 2027 by around $10 to $20 (via ITHome ). The source adds that this hike isn’t due to price-related pressures, but a company strategy to “regain control” of OLED panel pricing, which Samsung supposedly feels is “chaotic” right now.

title: My first Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 phone doesn’t live up to the hype
summary: More power than you need, but less than promised.
body: Credit: Robert Triggs / Android Authority When we first went hands-on with Qualcomm’s new Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 processor back in September, its headline features had me excited. With CPU clock speeds reaching 5GHz, a massive 16MB Oryon Flex Cache, and Qualcomm’s next-generation Adreno GPU, the chip promised a major leap in performance for demanding workloads such as emulation and gaming. Benchmarking Qualcomm’s Gen 6 Reference Phone backed up these promises. I’ve since spent the past week with the REDMAGIC 12 Pro , my first retail phone powered by Qualcomm’s new silicon. With 16GB of LPDDR5 RAM and a substantial active cooling system, it should deliver a compelling showcase of next-generation performance that you can actually buy.

title: Google Photos could soon show some more love to your RAW photos
summary: Finding RAW images in Google Photos could soon get a lot easier.
body: TL;DR Google is working on a new “RAW images” section in Google Photos’ Collections tab. This section will display all the RAW images backed up in Google Photos. The feature isn’t live right now, but we managed to surface it with some tinkering. Most Android phones these days can shoot RAW photos right out of the box. While that is great for image quality and offers better control while editing, RAW files also take up a lot of space. This can quickly turn into a problem when they begin eating into your Google account storage. It can also be difficult to find RAW photos in the app when you want to edit them. Fortunately, Google seems to be working to fix both those problems. You’re reading an Authority Insights story. title: Google Photos could finally learn to do your photo chores

Ask Photos lets you use natural language to ask complex questions about your library. You’d think it would help you organize your messy library , but it stops short after locating specific photos and videos, and that’s about it. That could soon change, as Ask Photos appears to be getting one of its biggest upgrades yet, one that could turn it into a full-fledged task engine, complete with a new overlay interface similar to Gemini’s. title: Another major Android brand wants your next phone to be wider, not taller
summary: Xiaomi is reportedly cooking a wide-screen slab phone.
body: Credit: Paul Jones / Android Authority TL;DR Xiaomi may be working on a wide-screen slab phone. The phone is rumored to come with a side-mounted fingerprint scanner. We’re unsure of the other details, but the same leaker previously claimed several wide phones from Chinese brands could arrive in 2027. Wide foldables are incredibly popular — far more than we expected. That popularity may also be driven by growing demand for smaller, but not less powerful, phones, as well as the proven convenience wider screens offer over tall phones in terms of usability. This growing demand now appears to fuel the creation of a new category of phones: wide-screen slab phones. According to leaker Digital Chat Station , Xiaomi is working on a slab phone with a wide screen, similar to the cover-screen dimensions of wide foldables such as the Galaxy Z Fold 8 and the iPhone Duo. While the leaker doesn’t divulge any other details, they add that it could include a side-mounted fingerprint scanner, which is more common on folding phones.

title: 9 things to do on day one to keep any foldable alive longer
summary: How to avoid mistakes that kill your foldable phone before its time.
body: Credit: Paul Jones / Android Authority Apple’s first foldable has had a rough start. Shortly after launch, iPhone Duo owners began reporting cracked inner screens , and Apple has since said the number of affected units will remain limited, pointing those affected to AppleCare for a screen replacement. It’s a reminder that, seven years after the first Galaxy Fold, foldables still ask a little more of their owners than slab phones do. The good news is that most of what keeps a foldable alive is habit, not luck. I’ve used a Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 6 for two years, and its hinge and inner screen are still in great shape. The crease has deepened a little after thousands of folds, but by no means excessively. I’ve also made a few embarrassing mistakes along the way. Here are nine things I’d do from day one with any foldable, whether it comes from Samsung, Apple, Google, or anyone else.

title: I loved the vivo X500 Pro Max, but one thing is holding it back from greatness
summary: The X500 Pro Max is a no-nonsense camera upgrade — but it'll cost you.
body: It’s Pro Max season, and like its fellow Chinese brethren, vivo couldn’t resist using iPhone-esque naming with the X500 Pro Max. If anything, the X500 Pro Max does a better job living up to its name, thanks to a bigger 6.85-inch panel, a 7,800mAh battery (6,750mAh in the EU), and all the extras you’d associate with a high-end Android phone in 2026. Other than that, though, you’re not going to see a huge difference from 2025’s X300 Pro (which this phone is the successor to, despite there also being an X500 Pro — I’ll explain this in the verdict I promise). While OPPO went with three 200MP cameras to make the Find X10 Pro Max stand out, vivo chose a more conservative path, focusing on iterative camera upgrades and tweaks to the tuning.

title: Don’t want Google using your Gmail or Photos info for ads? Here’s how to stop it
summary: Google created a loophole in its promise.
body: Credit: Pankil Shah / Android Authority “We don’t use your Gmail or Photos for ads” is one of Google’s longest-standing privacy promises. But with a recent policy change , that’s no longer entirely true. If you’ve turned on Personal Intelligence — the feature that lets Gemini and Search dig through your Gmail, Photos, and Drive for personalized answers — that same data can now shape the ads you see. Yes, it’s a big change, but thankfully, you have the option to opt out. Google’s Personal Intelligence now has a privacy cost

title: This treadmill owner used Claude to escape a subscription trap, and it’s glorious
summary: The results are making other treadmill owners take notice.
body: TL;DR A NordicTrack owner used Claude Code to escape iFIT’s subscription restrictions on their treadmill’s screen. The AI-assisted makeover added Netflix, Crunchyroll, and a custom workout interface without sacrificing essential controls. The owner has made the project public on GitHub for others who want to try something similar. A treadmill is supposed to make you sweat , not negotiate with a paywall. But NordicTrack apparently had other ideas, selling a machine with a big, beautiful screen that demands an iFIT subscription before it can become the entertainment hub you’ve paid for. One owner’s response? Call in Claude , evict the subscription headaches, and give the machine a second life. As detailed in a Reddit post, the owner’s girlfriend bought a NordicTrack Commercial 2250 a couple of years ago, with its large display as one of the biggest attractions. The couple wanted to enjoy Netflix and Crunchyroll while exercising, only to discover that accessing those services required an additional iFIT subscription, even though they already paid for the streaming services. Even basic workouts meant waiting for iFIT to load and dealing with its ads.

title: I tested the iPhone 18 Pro’s and Pixel 11 Pro’s photo styles, and there’s a clear winner
summary: The iPhone 18 Pro and Pixel 11 Pro take different approaches to photo filters. Here's why I prefer Apple's.
body: Credit: Stephen Radochia / Android Authority There’s no arguing that smartphone cameras have gotten really good. In fact, I believe that there are no bad cameras as far as flagships go, just different flavors. Sure, bigger sensors and better lenses help, but the key differentiator today is the processing, color science, and the level of control you get over images. To that effect, I spent the past month shooting with the iPhone 18 Pro and Google Pixel 11 Pro to see how their newfangled approaches to creative control compare. On the iPhone 18 Pro, Apple has reworked its Photographic Styles, giving you more control over the look and texture of your photos. Google, meanwhile, has introduced Camera Looks, a collection of presets that let you change the Pixel’s signature image processing.

title: Google is giving Chrome’s three-dot menu a much-needed brain
summary: No more digging through Chrome's endless menu options.
body: TL;DR Chrome’s redesigned three-dot menu now features a functional search box for finding browser actions, bookmarks, and recent history. Google is also experimenting with a scrollbar, pinned search field and footer, and cleaner, block-style menu sections. The redesign remains exclusive to Canary, with no confirmed stable release date. Chrome ‘s three-dot menu has always been a bit of a treasure hunt. You know the setting you’re looking for is buried somewhere in there, but finding it can mean scrolling through a maze of options or remembering which submenu Google decided to hide it under. Now, Google is working on a shortcut that could make all that digging unnecessary. And the latest Chrome Canary build shows it’s finally coming together. The latest development comes courtesy of Leopeva64 on X , who shared a demonstration of the now-functional search box in Chrome’s redesigned three-dot menu. Previously little more than a decorative placeholder, the search field can now pull up matching browser commands, bookmarks, and recently visited websites as you type.

title: Brace for more foldable phones with this form factor (if readers get their way)
summary: Microsoft called it. Samsung and Apple followed.
body: It’s been over seven years since we first welcomed foldable phones to the market, and since then, they’ve taken on various forms. Some worked really well, like the mainline Galaxy Z Fold series , while others have fallen to the wayside, like Microsoft’s Surface Duo. While the latter is still regarded as a bad bet on Microsoft’s part — and is, arguably, more a dual-screen device than a foldable — it did seemingly predict one notable trend. This year, we’ve seen the Galaxy Z Fold 8 and iPhone Duo adopt squatter form factors compared to devices before them, which raises the question: Do consumers prefer these short, squat screen aspect ratios over taller, narrower alternatives?

title: This app brings free internet radio to Android Auto, and it’s only getting better by the day
summary: RadioShake is completely free and doesn't even show ads.
body: TL;DR RadioShake is an internet radio app for Android Auto that supports over 45,000 radio stations. Its latest update introduces autoplay for your last played station and also improves song recognition. The app is completely free, has no ads, and doesn’t require an account. Listening to music is one of the many pleasures of going on a road trip. It can even make commuting to work easier. While there are a lot of music streaming apps where you can curate your own playlists, sometimes it’s just more fun to listen to the radio — especially if you have an internet radio app that lets you tune in to stations from around the world. That’s exactly what RadioShake was built for, and it’s only getting better with each update. The developer behind RadioShake built it “on the side” and has since pushed out regular updates with bug fixes and features requested by users. The developer has now announced v3.9 of the app, and it brings several new features. The app can now autoplay the last radio station you were listening to once your phone connects to Android Auto in your car. The feature is off by default and can be enabled in settings.

title: Something strange is happening with Android TV remotes, and it’s driving users crazy
summary: Android TV Home button no longer opens favorite apps for some.
body: TL;DR Some Android TV users report that pressing Home on the TV remote now selects the top navigation bar instead of their favorite apps. Reports span NVIDIA Shield TV devices, while our own observations suggest the behavior varies across Android TV hardware. Google hasn’t explained the apparent change, and we’re asking readers to help establish how widespread it is. There’s a special kind of frustration that comes from a button doing exactly what it says, just not what your fingers remember. For some Android TV owners, that button is Home, and a seemingly invisible change is sending their carefully rehearsed remote-control routines off-script. The mystery began when Android Authority’s Stephen Schenck noticed something strange while using his XGIMI Aura projector and an older JBL Link Bar. Pressing Home no longer brought up the familiar row of favorite apps. Instead, it jumped to the Home tab in the navigation bar above.

title: Google Photos now lets you stop Memories from ruining the mood
summary: You can finally stop the app from adding random music to your memories.
body: TL;DR Google Photos is finally getting a toggle to disable background music in Memories. Turning off the toggle disables background music on all Memories, including the End of Year Recap. It seems to be a server-side rollout, so you may have to wait for the feature to show up. I’ve always found Memories in Google Photos to be a useful and fun feature that often takes me back to the “good old days.” Whether it’s surfacing old clips of my friends and me from college or images from my first date with my wife, it’s usually great at showing the best moments of my life over the years. However, it sometimes adds the weirdest background music to Memories , which can pull you out of the experience. Fortunately, you can now stop that. Google today announced that it’s finally giving users the option to turn off background music in Memories. This means you won’t get random music tracks added to your Memories in Google Photos. For Memories that contain video, users will still hear the recorded audio.

title: Casio’s cute digital ring watch just got a successor
summary: Casio is back to deliver peak digital nostalgia straight to your finger.
body: Credit: Casio TL;DR Casio has launched a successor to its original ring watch. The CRW-002 can be set to a 12- or 24-hour format, offers stopwatch functionality, and is water resistant. It will be available this November in silver ($135) and in gold ($155). Casio did something novel in 2024, creating a digital watch in the form of a ring . It later went on to release a second ring watch that incorporated health tracking features. The company is back again with a new ring watch, but this time the device is a direct successor to the original. The design of the CRW-002 is based on the Casio A168 from 1995. It features an injection-molded metal casing and band with a mineral glass face. Under the glass is a seven-segment LCD screen that displays hours, minutes, and seconds. You’ll also find three working side buttons.

title: Chrome could soon make tab overload a lot easier to manage
summary: Finally catching up to Firefox.
body: TL;DR Google Chrome is testing a horizontally scrollable tab bar, making it easier to navigate dozens or hundreds of open tabs. Users can scroll through tabs using their mouse wheel or dedicated arrow buttons, while pinned tabs remain fixed on the left. The feature is currently available in Chrome Canary through an experimental flag, with no confirmed stable release date. Google Chrome is finally learning a trick that rivals like Firefox and Vivaldi have mastered for a few years now. Soon after (finally) giving us vertical tabs to stack all our open webpages neatly along the side, Chrome is learning a thing or two about making its traditional horizontal tab feel a lot more manageable, especially for those who keep several tabs open at once. The tech giant is testing a new horizontally scrollable tab bar, which should make it easier to navigate all open webpages once the tab strip fills up.

title: Reddit tests yet another change that absolutely no users want
summary: Soon, even your Reddit searches will have ads.
body: Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority TL;DR Reddit has announced that it is beginning to test placing ads in search result pages. The ads that appear will be based on a range of factors, including contextual relevance to a query. The test is being run with a select group of advertisers. Reddit recently announced controversial plans to shift primarily to a logged-in experience , which could change how people browse the website. On the heels of that divisive decision, Reddit has made another announcement that’s sure to rile up its users. You may soon start seeing more ads on the platform. In a blog post , the company revealed that it is beginning a new test. This test will see the insertion of ads on search result pages. Reddit says that it believes this area of the site has high purchase and search intent.

title: These muscle-reading wearables let you use voice input without speaking a word
summary: Forget glide typing — these glasses have maybe the best text-entry trick yet.
body: TL;DR Subvocal’s glasses tech uses radar to analyze the movement of muscles in your mouth. From those readings, it can extrapolate the words you’re saying — even if you’re just silently mouthing them. Pre-orders for the wearable are open now, with orders expected to ship in Q1 2027. Ever since mobile devices started getting smaller than a laptop, engineers have been tackling the difficult question of how we’re supposed to enter text. We’ve gone from tiny physical keyboards , to touchscreen keyboards, to gesture-based glide typing . On wearables, the situation’s even trickier, and it can feel like we’re stuck either using voice input or left awkwardly poking in the air at a virtual keyboard. But now one startup has a clever, hands-free solution that works silently. How many of you speak aloud to yourself as you type? Or maybe when proofreading, do you ever silently mouth the words as you’re reading them? You might be a prime candidate for trying out Subvocal’s glasses tech, which translates silent mouth movements into written text (via Hacker News ).

title: Google spent months pushing AI mode — now it might be doing the opposite
summary: Google was spotted testing Search without AI Mode.
body: TL;DR A user spotted Google testing Search without AI Mode on Chrome in Incognito mode. This follows a $500 million drop in Alphabet’s value due to underperforming ad revenue from AI Mode. It’s unclear if Google is limiting AI Mode for users it can’t make a profit from, or if it’s considering a return to stripped-down Search. When Google started its search business in 1998, it stated that its mission was “to organize the world’s information and make it universally accessible and useful.” Even though it still uses those words when it talks about Search, anyone who’s used AI Mode knows that it has strayed far from that original intent. Now there are signs that it might be ready to return to its roots. On X, Optimize My Firm CEO Len Raleigh posted a screenshot of Google sans AI Mode that he came across while using Incognito mode on Chrome (via Search Engine Roundtable ). He speculated that it was “[j]ust a test,” adding, “I still have AI Mode on other machines and on other sessions.” Search Engine Roundtable said it was not able to duplicate the result and neither were we at Android Authority .

title: Smart homes are in disarray after daylight saving time baffles Google Nest devices (Update)
summary: Nest Thermostats and Hubs are stumbling over the daylight saving time shift.
